title: Linda Arthur
text:
I am data professional and a Master’s student in Data Science at the University of British Columbia (UBC).
My journey has taken me from studying Computer Science at Ashesi University in Ghana to working across technology, research, product management, and data analysis. I am particularly interested in how data and technology can be used to address real-world challenges.
Through the UBC Master of Data Science program, I am developing stronger skills in statistical analysis, machine learning, data visualization, and computational problem-solving.
Explore the site to learn more about me, my background, interests, and the work I hope to do with data.

title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
Week 1: Getting Started with MDS
My first week of the Master of Data Science (MDS) program has been exciting and full of new experiences. I have spent the week learning new concepts, getting familiar with the program, and meeting new people.
One of the things I have enjoyed most so far is making new friends and connecting with other students. Starting a new program in a new environment can be challenging, so having people around who are also learning and experiencing the same things has made the transition more enjoyable.
Academically, I am particularly happy that I am beginning to understand the basics of probability. Some of the concepts were initially challenging, but as I worked through the material and practiced more, they started to make sense. This has given me more confidence as I continue building my foundation in data science.
It is only the first week, so there is still a lot to learn. However, I am excited about the journey ahead and looking forward to seeing how much I will grow throughout the program.
Week 1 takeaway: Keep learning, keep asking questions, and don’t be afraid of difficult concepts. They become easier with practice.

title: About
text:
I am a Computer Science graduate from Ashesi University in Ghana, where I developed an interest in using technology to solve practical problems. My undergraduate experience gave me a foundation in software development, databases, data analysis, and problem-solving.
Since graduating, I have had the opportunity to work in different environments, including technology, research, product management, and social impact. These experiences have helped me understand that technology is most valuable when it is connected to real problems and the people affected by them.

title: About
text:
My Journey into Data Science
My interest in data science grew from seeing how data can help us understand problems that are otherwise difficult to see.
I have worked with tools such as Python, R, SQL, Excel, Tableau, and Power BI, and I have applied data analysis to research and organizational problems. My research experience has also exposed me to survey design, data cleaning, statistical analysis, and communicating findings to different audiences.
I chose to pursue the Master of Data Science at UBC because I want to move beyond simply working with data toward developing the technical and analytical skills needed to build reliable, data-driven solutions.

title: About
text:
Areas I Care About
I am particularly interested in the intersection of data science, environmental health, and public health.
One area I have been exploring is the relationship between landfill air pollution, extreme weather, and respiratory health in Ghana. I am interested in how data from different sources—such as environmental, climate, geographic, and health data—can be combined to better understand these relationships.
I am also interested in using data science to help African organizations and businesses make better decisions, especially organizations that may not yet have the resources or expertise to fully use their data.

title: About
section: What I Hope to Learn at UBC
text:
What I Hope to Learn at UBC
During my MDS journey, I hope to strengthen my ability to:
Analyze and interpret complex datasets Build statistical and machine-learning models Work with spatial and temporal data Communicate data-driven insights clearly Develop reproducible and responsible data workflows Use data science to address real-world problems
Beyond the technical skills, I also want to become better at asking the right questions before choosing a model or analyzing a dataset.

title: About
text:
Looking Ahead
My long-term goal is to use data and technology to contribute to meaningful development in Africa.
I hope to work at the intersection of data science, technology, research, and social impact—helping organizations turn data into information that can support better decisions and better outcomes.
This website will document part of that journey: what I learn, what I build, and how my thinking develops throughout the MDS program.
